issue: The lesson, flashcard f5 and aud-rm-17 teach "clearly trivial" as a purely quantitative cut-off: anything below the threshold need not be accumulated. The module's own TBS aud-tbs-u3-risk-materiality (row qual.u3) correctly scores a $7,000 misstatement below the $8,000 threshold as "Accumulate and evaluate" because it lets the entity meet a debt covenant. A student who learned the rule from the lesson, card or MCQ will get that TBS row wrong.
evidence: Lesson takeaway (line 36): "Misstatements below the clearly trivial threshold need not be accumulated." f5 back: "Misstatements below it are clearly inconsequential, individually and in aggregate, and need not be accumulated." aud-rm-17 key "No" with explanation "misstatements that are clearly trivial needn't be accumulated", answering a stem about misstatements "below the clearly trivial threshold". AU-C 450.A2-A3: clearly trivial is judged "by any criteria of size, nature, or circumstances", and when there is any uncertainty the matter is treated as not clearly trivial. So an amount below the threshold is not automatically clearly trivial. TBS u3 qual.u3 key = "Accumulate and evaluate" ($7,000 < $8,000 CT, covenant effect).
fix: Lesson takeaway: "Misstatements below the clearly trivial threshold need not be accumulated, unless their nature or circumstances (e.g., a covenant, fraud) make them more than inconsequential; if in doubt, accumulate." f5 back: add "unless qualitative factors (nature or circumstances) make them not clearly trivial". aud-rm-17: reword the stem to "...below the clearly trivial threshold, with no qualitative factors present?", or keep the stem and add the qualifier to the key explanation.

issue: Four single-fact recall items are labeled analysis or evaluation with difficulty 3. That is two to three skill levels too high. It inflates the module's analysis and evaluation counts, which feed the Blueprint skill-mix targets.
evidence: aud-rm-24 (analysis/3): "IR and CR both high -> detection risk must be low" is the same one-step relationship as aud-x2-38, which is labeled remembering/1. aud-rm-25 (analysis/3, calc:true): "PM $75,000 -> TM up to $75,000" only requires recalling TM <= PM; there is no computation. aud-rm-26 (evaluation/3): "RMM rises -> modify planned procedures" is recall of AU-C 315. aud-rm-27 (evaluation/3): "controls over a significant risk relied on -> test in the current period" is recall of AU-C 330.15. Blueprint definitions: Analysis = examining interrelationships to identify causes and support inferences; Evaluation = examining and judging the outcomes of analysis. None of these items requires either. Practice+exam mix as labeled: R11/A17/An4/E3 (31/49/11/9%). As corrected by this review (this finding plus the one-level mislabels): R20/A14/An0/E1 (57/40/0/3%). The Blueprint ranges are R&U 30-40, App 30-40, An 15-25, Eval 5-15.
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill definitions and AUD skill allocation (review/reference/blueprint-notes.md); AU-C 315; AU-C 330.15; AU-C 530.A11
fix: Relabel aud-rm-24, -25, -26 and -27 as skill remembering, difficulty 1, and set calc:false on aud-rm-25. Separately, write two or three genuine analysis or evaluation items for this module, for example: compare three assertions' IR/CR tables to rank the needed persuasiveness; evaluate whether revised materiality after actual results makes the completed sample sizes insufficient.

issue: Skill and difficulty are one level too high on several items. Recall items are labeled application. Simple applications are labeled analysis/3.
evidence: Labeled application but pure recall (should be remembering): aud-rm-chk1 (its twin aud-x2-38 is labeled remembering), aud-rm-09 (an understanding of IC is always required), aud-rm-16 (identical to aud-rm-chk2, labeled remembering), aud-rm-17, aud-rm-18 (NFP benchmark), aud-rm-20 (TM based on PM). aud-rm-16, -17, -18 and -20 are also difficulty 2 although they need one fact. Labeled analysis/3 but single-step application: aud-rm-14 (5% x 1,200,000 = 60,000; the same concept as aud-rm-07, which is labeled application/2) and aud-rm-19 (choose a stable benchmark when earnings are volatile).
fix: Set chk1, rm-09, rm-16, rm-17, rm-18 and rm-20 to remembering (difficulty 1 for rm-16, -17, -18 and -20). Set rm-14 and rm-19 to application, difficulty 2.

issue: The lesson does not teach several AU-C 320/450 rules that this module's own items test. No other AUD lesson teaches them either, so a learner who misses these items is routed back to a lesson that does not contain the answer. The gaps are Blueprint Area II.D (materiality for the FS as a whole; tolerable misstatement and performance materiality).
evidence: Searched all content/aud/modules/*/lesson.md. (1) Benchmark selection (NFP -> total revenue or expenses; volatile or breakeven earnings -> revenue, assets or normalized income; asset-based entities): only "e.g., pretax income from continuing operations" (line 35); "not-for-profit" appears in no materiality context. Tested by aud-rm-18, aud-rm-19 and aud-x2-06; only aud-rm-04's explanation lists benchmarks. (2) Lower materiality for particular classes, balances or disclosures (AU-C 320.10): the phrase "particular class" appears in no lesson. Tested by aud-rm-13 and aud-x2-07. (3) Tolerable misstatement: the lesson only says "lower tolerable misstatement" in the Extent row; there is no definition and no link to PM. Tested by aud-rm-20 and aud-rm-25 (aud-sampling, a later unit, defines it). (4) Factual, judgmental and projected misstatements (AU-C 450.A6): "factual" appears in no lesson. Tested by aud-tbs-x8-materiality c1-c3.
source: AU-C 320.10, .A8 (benchmarks); AU-C 530.05/.A11 (tolerable misstatement); AU-C 450.A6 (types of misstatements); AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint Area II.D
fix: Add a short "Choosing the benchmark" table to the Materiality section: for-profit stable -> pretax income from continuing operations; volatile or breakeven -> normalized income, revenue or total assets; NFP -> total revenue or total expenses; asset-based -> total assets or net assets. State that these are illustrative, not required. Add one paragraph on specific (lower) materiality for sensitive items such as related-party disclosures or executive compensation (AU-C 320.10). Add one sentence defining tolerable misstatement as the application of PM to a sampling procedure, set at or below PM. In the AU-C 450 paragraph, add factual, judgmental and projected misstatements with one example each.

issue: Three items tagged to this module (unit aud-u3) test rules that are first taught in later units. The lesson also uses the term "significant risk" (lines 114-115; aud-rm-08; f6) without ever defining it, so misses route to a lesson that does not cover them.
evidence: aud-rm-09 (an understanding of IC is required even with CR at maximum) is taught in aud-internal-control (aud-u4). aud-rm-27 (controls over significant risks must be tested in the current period) is taught in aud-tests-of-controls lesson line 32 (aud-u5). aud-x2-26 (SAS 145 spectrum of inherent risk) is taught in aud-understanding-entity lines 34 and 64 (aud-u4). In aud.yaml, aud-risk-materiality precedes all three modules.
fix: Retag moduleId to aud-internal-control (rm-09), aud-tests-of-controls (rm-27) and aud-understanding-entity (x2-26). Alternatively, add one sentence to the lesson: "A significant risk is one whose inherent risk is assessed near the upper end of the spectrum (or that a standard designates, such as management override); see Understanding the entity."

issue: TBS moduleIds omit the module that teaches part of each simulation, so misses are not routed to the right lesson.
evidence: x3 part "law" (AU-C 250, direct- vs indirect-effect laws) is taught only in aud-specific-risks; x3 moduleIds = [aud-risk-materiality, aud-understanding-entity, aud-fraud-risk]. x8 row "war" (a misstatement measured to the nearest end of the auditor's range) is taught in aud-specific-risks lesson lines 60-72; x8 moduleIds = [aud-risk-materiality] only.
fix: Add "aud-specific-risks" to moduleIds in both aud-tbs-x3-risk and aud-tbs-x8-materiality.

issue: Exam-pool (mock) items reuse the exact figures of the lesson's worked example or a practice TBS. Learners can recognize the answers, which inflates mock scores.
evidence: aud-x2-25: $2,000,000 x 5% x 75% = 100,000 / 75,000, identical to the lesson's worked example (lines 122-131). aud-tbs-x3-risk: $4,000,000, 5%, 70% -> 200,000 / 140,000, identical to practice aud-tbs-r3-detection-risk. aud-tbs-x8-materiality: $3,200,000, 5%, CT 5% -> 160,000 / 8,000, identical to practice aud-tbs-u3-risk-materiality; both clients are "...Foods".
fix: Change the exam figures. For example: x2-25 pretax income $2,400,000 with PM 70% (-> 120,000 / 84,000); x3 pretax income $3,600,000 (-> 180,000 / 126,000), keeping the CEO bonus threshold equal to reported income; x8 pretax income $2,800,000 (-> 140,000 / 98,000 / 7,000), then re-check that the aggregate of 135,000 still falls below materiality, or rescale the misstatements.

issue: Numeric distractor rationales do not name the error that produces the number, and some trap labels do not fit.
evidence: Python reproduction from the stems: aud-rm-14 (c) $120,000 = 10% x 1,200,000 (wrong percentage applied to actual income), but its explanation says "Lower income lowers materiality" and the trap is wrong-sign; the only "increase" route (5% of the original $2,000,000) gives $100,000, which is option (b). aud-rm-25 (c) $25,000 = 100,000 - 75,000 and (d) $175,000 = 100,000 + 75,000, explained only as "That is not the limit." and "Not the computation.". aud-x2-25 (c) $150,000 cannot be produced by any natural error (100,000/0.75 = 133,333; 100,000 x 1.75 = 175,000; 2,000,000 x 5% = 100,000), yet it is labeled wrong-sign with the generic rationale "Performance materiality is less than materiality."
source: Batch procedure: reproduce each numeric distractor
fix: rm-14 (c): change it to "$100,000 x 1,200,000/2,000,000..." or, simpler, explain (c) as "applies 10% to actual income; the benchmark percentage does not change" with trap distractor-number. rm-25 (c)/(d): explain them as "the gap between overall and performance materiality, not a limit" and "adds the two thresholds". x2-25 (c): replace it with $133,333 (= 100,000 / 0.75, "divides by 75% instead of multiplying", trap reversed).

issue: Trap labels do not match the misconception the distractor models.
evidence: aud-rm-01 (d) "After considering controls but before substantive procedures" is the definition of RMM, a different risk (wrong-classification), not partial-computation. aud-rm-20 (c) "The clearly trivial amount" contains no number, so distractor-number does not fit; it is wrong-classification. aud-rm-27 (a) "Every third year" and (d) "Never; trust last year" model the rotation / prior-year-evidence rule (wrong-period), not wrong-classification. aud-x2-06 (b) "A first-year audit" is relevant (initial audits usually push materiality or PM down), so irrelevant-fact is wrong; it is reversed.
fix: rm-01 d -> wrong-classification; rm-20 c -> wrong-classification; rm-27 a,d -> wrong-period; x2-06 b -> reversed, with the explanation "First-year audits carry more risk and usually lead to lower, not higher, materiality."

issue: Practice items 13-27 have telegraphic, near-circular explanations that do not state the rule or why the option is wrong. Some item-level explanations also omit the computation or the authority.
evidence: Examples: rm-17 "That isn't required." (twice), "That isn't what the rule says."; rm-21 "That is not the model." (three times); rm-22 "Not the components." (twice); rm-23 "It's the entity's." (three times); rm-24 "It suggests the opposite.", "That is not related."; rm-26 "Not appropriate.", "That is not required."; rm-27 "Not for significant risks." (twice); rm-19 "Not representative."; rm-18 key "Correct. Profit isn't the focus."; rm-16 "That's a separate amount."; rm-20 "That's too low."; rm-15 "Its qualitative effect matters."; rm-13 "Disclosures are subject to materiality.". rm-14's item explanation never shows 1,200,000 x 5% = 60,000. rm-25 cites no AU-C 530 rule. By contrast, rm-01 to rm-12 explain each option properly.
fix: Rewrite each distractor explanation to name the rule, matching the style of rm-01 to rm-12. For example, rm-21 (b): "Adds instead of multiplies, and leaves out detection risk; AR = IR x CR x DR." rm-27 (a): "The every-third-audit rotation applies only to unchanged controls that do not address a significant risk (AU-C 330.14)." Add "Revised: 5% x 1,200,000 = $60,000" to rm-14, and "AU-C 530: TM is PM applied to a sample, at or below PM" to rm-25.
